Nina (AE): Quick heads-up — Prospect (Theo from FirstTrust Bank) asked for an on-prem POC + customer-managed KEK with warm failover semantics. They want a pen-test window and a clear SLA delta if we route to proxy HSMs.
Priya (Solutions Eng): Got it. Can you paste their specific asks? e.g., rotation cadence, failover RTO/RPO, and whether they need attestation?
Nina (AE): Paste from email: "Require weekly KEK rotation (can be scheduled), warm-failover across 2 HSM regions, pen-test window of 4 weeks pre-prod, and proof of attestation during failover. Also need cost delta for reserved vs burst capacity while failing over."
Dan (Security): Pen-test window OK but we need to confirm scope: network egress, API auth, and HSM proxy attestation. Also need their SOC2 evidence before we start.
Theo (Customer): Correct — we'll provide SOC2 + ISO docs. Pen-test must include HSM proxy handshake and KEK rotation dry-run. Can you confirm network ports and IP allowlist?
Marta (SRE): For warm failover we'll need a ~90s topology shift for KV cache cold start unless we use prefix caching. Expect a short latency spike. Can we document fallback policy?
Priya (Solutions Eng): Options: 1) Active-active with synchronous replication (higher cost, <500ms switch). 2) Active-passive warm failover with KV warming (90s spike). I'll map cost/latency tradeoffs.
Nina (AE): Customer also asked about billing model during failover: do we charge burst rates immediately or amortize across reserved pool?
Priya (Solutions Eng): We usually apply reserved capacity first; burst billing triggers if reserved exhausted. I'll get precise pricing delta for multi-region HSM proxy egress.
Dan (Security): Rotation specifics: do they want customer to hold KEK in their HSM (BYO) or have Redwood manage envelope keys with customer CMK in HSM? This changes attestation path.
Theo (Customer): Prefer customer-held CMK in our proxy HSM (we provision attested tokens). Need to ensure rotation procedure doesn't expose plaintext to Redwood.
Priya (Solutions Eng): That is doable via an HSM handshake where we only receive wrapped keys. We have a standard flow: \n```\n1) Customer generates KEK in their HSM\n2) Wrap model key (DEK) with KEK\n3) Send wrapped DEK over TLS\n4) Redwood stores wrapped DEK; unwrap happens only inside customer's HSM via proxy during inference\n```
Priya (Solutions Eng): NOTE: if unwrapping happens in-customer HSM via proxy, latency will depend on HSM call latency ~10-50ms per call, and we can cache unwrapped DEKs for session TTL to avoid repeated calls.
Marta (SRE): Cache TTL tradeoff: 5 min TTL reduces HSM calls but widens blast radius if KEK rotation occurs. Need to agree on TTL in design docs.
Dan (Security): For pen-test, we require read-only access to logs for the period, and a signed attestation artifact from the HSM vendor when we run the failover test.
Nina (AE): Action items: Priya to provide pricing delta + architecture note; Marta to list operational impacts and recommended TTLs; Dan to list pen-test scope and attestation checklist. Theo will confirm SOC2 drop and pen-test dates.
Theo (Customer): We can do pen-test week of 1779994000 (approx). Will confirm IPs and SOC2 by EOD.
Priya (Solutions Eng): I'll draft a short runbook and an example failover timeline (including curl examples for testing) by EOD tomorrow. e.g., `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keystore/status`
infra-bot: Created doc: /runbooks/sales/firsttrust-kek-warm-failover.md (internal link) :page_with_curl: 
Marta (SRE): Also note: if we use synchronous replication, billing delta ~+40% on reserved cost (back-of-envelope). I'll confirm precise numbers.
Dan (Security): One blocker: Legal needs a clause for customer-keystore key-responsibility and pen-test indemnity. I'll loop in Legal if Theo confirms pen-test.
Nina (AE): Thanks all — I'll update the customer thread with the next steps and timelines. Keep threads here for any blockers. :thumbsup:
